migrationCompatibility.notes: Presentation and copy only. No schema change, no API contract movement. This is the last-mile defence and is deliberately independent of the source-side fix; the two can land in either order.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: repoint the nginx demo upstream to the retained previous release; the run view reverts whole, never half-applied

doNotInfer: dictionary.md's _Avoid_ field is SPLIT ON COMMAS. A comma inside a parenthetical produces inert fragments that match nothing and silently disable the guard — this cost #1956 a red CI round, twice in one file. Put rationale in Definition, never in _Avoid_. Then PRINT the parsed aliases and confirm each is a clean standalone string; do not infer correctness from the file text.

Do NOT edit packages/contracts/seller-copy-banned-patterns.json. It is shared with the Python agent guard and a Latin-script heuristic there would false-positive on brand names. A test asserts it is unchanged.
All 33 existing banned patterns were run against the offending string and matched ZERO. Do not assume the shared list gives any coverage here; this guard must be surface-local to apps/demo.
describeOptionField's raw-key fallback is deliberate elsewhere. Changing it is in scope for THIS surface only — do not alter callers outside the run surface.
The rationale guard must not depend on the payload having been fixed upstream. It is defence in depth at the last place before a seller reads the text.
New dictionary entries need all four of EN, VI, _Avoid_ and Definition.
Pin PYTHONPATH="$PWD/backend/src:$PWD" for any pytest run inside the worktree, or the green is fake.
